topics.description: A Sicilian organized-crime network commonly known as Cosa Nostra or La Cosa Nostra.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Frank Sheeran recounted his supposed murder of a leader of this union in his memoir I Heard You Paint Houses. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this union led by Jimmy Hoffa, who mysteriously disappeared in 1975.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This man rose to prominence by questioning Hoffa during the McClellan Committee hearings. This man was shot at the Ambassador Hotel five years after his brother was shot in Dallas.
parts.answer: Robert F. Kennedy [accept RFK; prompt on Kennedy; DO NOT ACCEPT OR PROMPT ON JFK]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hoffa’s disappearance was linked to this organized crime syndicate, known as La Cosa Nostra. The Corleone family in The Godfather was partially based on this organization’s Genovese family.
parts.answer: the Sicillian Mafia [or the Mob; accept La Cosa Nostra before it is read]

topics.description: The modern country in northeastern Africa and the Middle East, centered on the Nile Valley and Delta and including the Sinai Peninsula and Suez Canal.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Tale of Two Brothers centers on this god’s relationship with his brother Bata. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this jackal-headed god of mummification and death. This son of Nephthys (NEF-this) weighed the souls of the dead to determine whether they were worthy of entering the realm of the dead.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Anubis is a key deity in the mythology of this country. Rulers from this country were buried in pyramids to ensure their safe passage to the afterlife.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In the Hall of Two Truths, Anubis weighed the hearts of the dead against one of these objects belonging to Ma’at.

topics.description: The ancient Nile Valley civilization ruled by pharaohs, including the unified kingdoms of Upper and Lower Egypt.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One ruler of this country, Hor-Aha, died after being carried off during a hunt by a hippo. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this country, whose “Upper” and “Lower” regions were unified by one of its pharaohs, Narmer.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Hor-Aha politely named a year the “Year of the Smiting of [this region]” after leading a campaign against it. This region directly south of Egypt was later ruled by the Kingdom of Kush.
parts.answer: Nubia [or the “Year of the Smiting of Nubia;” prompt on Sudan]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Hor-Aha is possibly conflated with Narmer on the prehistoric king list on the Palermo Stone, which is named for the capital of this triangular island in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: According to Herodotus, the first female ruler of this civilization was the semi-mythical empress Nitocris, whom Herodotus associated with Menkaure. This civilization was ruled from Amarna by the husband of Nefertiti. Another female ruler of this civilization, Hatshepsut, wore masculine clothing to represent the sun god Ra. For ten points, name this ancient African civilization that ruled the area around the Nile river.
parts.answer: ancient Egyptians (accept Old Kingdom before “Amarna” is read)

topics.description: The 1618 incident in which Bohemian Protestant rebels threw imperial representatives from a window, helping trigger the Thirty Years' War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The number “135797531” (read the individual digits) was carved near a bridge in this city to  mark the moment when Charles IV (the fourth) began its construction. Ottokar I (oh-tah-KAR the  first) of the Přemyslid (PREM-iz-lid) dynasty reigned from this city, in whose outskirts Frederick V  (the fifth) the Winter King lost the throne at the Battle of (*) White Mountain. The theologian Jan  Hus (yahn hoos) spent much of his life in this city. The Thirty Years War began after officials were  thrown out windows in the second “defenestration of” this city. For 10 points, name this most populous  Bohemian and Czech city.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The death of Bogislaw XIV during this war resulted in one belligerent annexing his state under the Treaty of Stettin. The War of the Mantuan Succession was a part of this larger conflict which featured the brutal sack of Magdeburg. The Treaty of Lübeck ended Christian IV’s involvement with one side in this war. Count Tilly won the battle of (*) White Mountain during this war’s Bohemian phase, which began after Ferdinand II’s representatives were thrown out of a window in the Second Defenestration of Prague. For 10 points, what large European war between Catholic and Protestant forces was ended by the Peace of Westphalia after three decades of fighting?

topics.description: The 1991 U.S.-led military operation that attacked Iraq and drove Iraqi forces from Kuwait during the Gulf War.

parts.label: L
parts.question: After invading a neighboring nation, this man threatened to launch the “mother of all battles.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this dictator who was captured in a “spider hole” during the 2003 invasion of Iraq. The toppling of the Firdos Square statue of this dictator was broadcast live and symbolically ended his government.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Hussein had invaded Kuwait in 1991 after accusing them of breaking OPEC’s production quotas of this good. Retreating Iraqi troops caused an environmental disaster by burning over 700 wells that produced this good.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] “Stormin’” Norman Schwarzkopf led this portion of the Gulf War, which included the attack on Iraq. This operation followed the liberation of Kuwait and Operation Desert Shield.

topics.description: The 1990–1991 international conflict in which a U.S.-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait after Iraq’s invasion.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this body of water, Harra trees are native to mangroves on the island of Qeshm. Oil fields in this body of water were the subject of a 1990s war named after it. One country has built stadiums overlooking this body of water for the 2022 World Cup. This body of water is connected to the Gulf of (*) Oman by the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain is completely surrounded by, for 10 points, what gulf named after the ancient name for Iran?
parts.answer: Persian Gulf [accept Persian Gulf War; prompt on Gulf War]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Ironically, violence escalated in this country after a president gave a speech about it under a "Mission Accomplished" banner. Because of tensions over oil, this country invaded its neighbor to begin the First Gulf War. In 1980 this country invaded (*) Iran under the leadership of Saddam Hussein. The terrorist group ISIS is named for Syria and, for 10 points, what country led from Baghdad?

topics.description: The collaborationist French government led by Philippe Pétain from Vichy under German influence during World War II.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The launch of this military campaign ended an eight-month period of relative inaction dubbed  the “Phony War.” Maxime Weygand's (max-EEM VAY-gah's) planned counterattack failed to stop  this campaign. The Second Armistice at Compiègne (kahm-PEN-yeh) was signed just six weeks  after the start of this campaign, which took a route through the (*) Ardennes (ARD-en) Forest that  bypassed the Maginot (MAA-jin-oh) Line and led to the creation of the Vichy (VEE-shee) government.  For 10 points, name this World War II Nazi-led campaign whose outcome forced Charles de Gaulle  (SHARL day GOAL) to flee to Britain.
parts.answer: Battle of France [or German invasion of France; or Axis defeat of France in World War  II; or Nazi invasion of France until “Nazi” is read]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This government adopted the motto, “Work, Family, Fatherland” and was led by Philippe Pétain. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this collaborationist puppet government that was established under duress from Germany in July 1940.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This fascist German political party led by Adolf Hitler installed and controlled the Vichy government in France.
parts.answer: Nazi Party (accept National Socialist German Workers’ Party)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This politician and general opposed the Vichy government, instead leading Free France during World War II. He later established the Fifth Republic in France.
parts.answer: Charles de Gaulle (accept Charles André Joseph Marie de Gaulle)

topics.description: Gaius Marius was a Roman general and statesman who served as consul seven times and became a major figure in the late Roman Republic's civil conflicts.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Armies under this consul stopped the Cimbri (KIM-bree) and Teutones (too-TOH-nayz) at the Battles  of Aquae Sextiae (AK-wai SEXT-ee-ai) and Vercellae (vair-KEL-ai). For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this “third founder of Rome,” who became consul for the seventh time in the midst of a civil  conflict against his former colleague in the Jugurthine (jug-UR-theen) War.
parts.answer: Gaius Marius [The colleague referred to is Sulla.]

parts.label: B
parts.question: After serving as governor of Hispania Ulterior, Marius married Julia, the aunt of this dictator who  carried on much of Marius's program before being killed on the Ides of March.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Marius was exiled during a power struggle in this 91 BC conflict, in which Italian allies of Rome  rebelled over a lack of citizenship rights.
parts.answer: Social War [or Marsic War; or War of the Allies; prompt on Italian War]

topics.description: A Daoist-inspired peasant rebellion led by Zhang Jue against the Eastern Han Dynasty in the second century CE.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Along with an army under the White Banner, armies that used banners of this color were the most prestigious in the Manchu Army. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this color that partially names a Han Dynasty peasant revolt led by the Taoist mystic Zhang Jue [jung jway].

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] A dragon on a yellow field was the flag of this Chinese dynasty. Puyi was the last emperor of this dynasty, which was succeeded by the Republic of China.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] In modern times, the color yellow in China has been associated with these objects used by Hong Kong protesters. These namesakes of a 2014 “Movement” have been used to shield protesters from tear gas.
parts.answer: umbrellas [or parasols; accept Yellow Umbrella Movement]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This dynasty was briefly interrupted by Wang Mang’s Xin Dynasty. The Records of the Grand Historian was written during this dynasty, which was founded by Liu Bang after the fall of the Qin Dynasty. This dynasty was weakened by the (*) Yellow Turban Rebellion, leading to the tumultuous Three Kingdoms Period. For 10 points, what Chinese dynasty shares its name with China’s majority ethnic group?

topics.description: Idi Amin Dada was a Ugandan military officer and dictator who ruled Uganda from 1971 to 1979.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of this leader’s self-bestowed titles called him “Lord of All the Beasts of the Earth and Fishes of the Seas.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this erratic and allegedly cannibalistic African dictator who overthrew Milton Obote to come to power in 1971.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Amin faced the Entebbe Raid after he harbored members of the PFLP, who committed this type of crime by unlawfully seizing an airplane.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Another of Amin’s self-bestowed titles called him the conqueror of this empire, whose former African colonies include Egypt and Sudan.
parts.answer: British Empire [accept United Kingdom or Great Britain] <World History–Kapadia>

parts.label: L
parts.question: The use of mass internment in response to this rebellion is discussed in Caroline Elkins’ 2005 book Imperial Reckoning. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this event that saw the Land and Freedom Army fight against British rule under the leadership of Dedan Kimathi and General China. The Kapenguria Six were put on trial for being the purported ringleaders of this event.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The Mau Mau uprising took place in this east African country. Many British colonists settled in this country’s capital of Nairobi during the colonial period.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This Ugandan dictator participated in the Mau Mau uprising as an officer in the King’s African Rifles. This dictator was forced out of power after a failed invasion of Tanzania in the Kagera War.
